root/riboviria/orthornavirae/kitrinoviri.name: Flaviviridae
root/riboviria/orthornavirae/kitrinoviri.note: Positive-sense, non-segmented RNA viruses. The genus Orthoflavivirus divides ecologically into mosquito-borne, tick-borne and no-known-vector clades, and antigenically into serocomplexes. Cross-reactive antibody is the central diagnostic problem of the family, and the mechanism behind antibody-dependent enhancement in dengue.

root/riboviria/orthornavirae/negarnaviri.name: Hantaviridae
root/riboviria/orthornavirae/negarnaviri.note: Rodent-, shrew-, mole- and bat-borne bunyavirals. Unlike most bunyavirals they are not arthropod-borne: humans are infected by inhaling aerosolised rodent excreta. Each virus is tied to one reservoir species, so the geography of human disease follows small-mammal distributions. Old World viruses cause HFRS, New World viruses cause hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome.

highlights.name: Orthohantavirus andesense
highlights.headline: The only hantavirus with firmly documented person-to-person transmission.

highlights.name: Orthohantavirus hantanense
highlights.headline: Prototype hantavirus and cause of the severe form of haemorrhagic fever with renal syndrome (HFRS) in East Asia.

highlights.name: Orthohantavirus puumalaense
highlights.headline: Cause of nephropathia epidemica, the mild form of HFRS and the most common hantavirus disease in Europe.

highlights.name: Orthohantavirus sinnombreense
highlights.headline: Cause of hantavirus cardiopulmonary syndrome in North America, identified during the 1993 Four Corners outbreak.

root/riboviria/orthornavirae/negarnaviri.name: Peribunyaviridae
root/riboviria/orthornavirae/negarnaviri.note: Tri-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses (L, M, S). The segmented genome permits reassortment between co-infecting strains, which has repeatedly generated new human pathogens — Ngari virus (haemorrhagic fever in East Africa) and Iquitos virus arose this way. The family contains the genus Orthobunyavirus, whose >130 species are traditionally sorted into about 22 serogroups defined by cross-neutralisation.

root/riboviria/orthornavirae/negarnaviri.name: Arenaviridae
root/riboviria/orthornavirae/negarnaviri.note: Bi-segmented ambisense RNA viruses. Mammarenaviruses are rodent-borne, split into Old World (Lassa, LCMV) and New World clades A–C; clade B contains the South American haemorrhagic fever viruses (Junín, Machupo, Guanarito, Sabiá, Chapare). Reservoir specificity again dictates the geography of human disease.

root/riboviria/orthornavirae/negarnaviri.name: Nairoviridae
root/riboviria/orthornavirae/negarnaviri.note: Tick-borne bunyavirals with unusually large L segments. The genus Orthonairovirus contains Crimean-Congo haemorrhagic fever virus — the most widely distributed tick-borne human pathogen — alongside many serogroups known only from ticks and seabird colonies.

root/riboviria/orthornavirae/pisuviricot.name: Coronaviridae
root/riboviria/orthornavirae/pisuviricot.note: Large positive-sense RNA viruses with a 5'-capped, polyadenylated genome and prominent spike glycoprotein. Seven species infect humans: four seasonal (229E, NL63, OC43, HKU1) and three of high consequence (SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV, SARS-CoV-2). Bats are the ancestral reservoir for alpha- and betacoronaviruses.

root/riboviria/orthornavirae/pisuviricot.note: Small non-enveloped positive-sense RNA viruses. Enterovirus alone accounts for polioviruses, coxsackieviruses, echoviruses, EV-A71, EV-D68 and the rhinoviruses — collectively the commonest human viral infections.

highlights.name: Deltaretrovirus priTlym1
highlights.headline: The first human retrovirus discovered, infecting 5-10 million people. Most carry it for life without consequence; a minority develop adult T-cell leukaemia/lymphoma after decades, or a progressive myelopathy.

highlights.name: Lentivirus humimdef1
highlights.headline: Retrovirus causing AIDS; roughly 40 million people live with HIV and antiretroviral therapy has transformed it into a manageable chronic infection.

highlights.name: Lentivirus humimdef2
highlights.headline: A West African lentivirus from sooty mangabeys, less transmissible and slower to progress than HIV-1, and intrinsically resistant to two whole antiretroviral classes.

highlights.name: Orthohepadnavirus hominoidei
highlights.headline: 254 million people live with chronic hepatitis B, and it is a vaccine-preventable cause of cirrhosis and liver cancer that treatment controls but does not cure.
